propositions: Root disk on autodeploy host fills to 92–96% and remains pinned during quiescent main because prune_docker_caches is only called on deploy and backoff paths, not on the no-op early exit that fires every ~2 minutes
The no-op exit path (autodeploy.sh:228) must call a pressure-triggered prune to reclaim disk between deploys when main is idle
prune_docker_caches is currently defined after the no-op exit (line 228) and must be relocated before it so the function is defined when called
A throttled reclaim triggered at root disk >= 80% (configurable) with a 600-second minimum interval prevents churn while maintaining a warm 5GB builder cache
Pressure-path prune failures are non-fatal and only log; they do not alter the script's exit code or control flow
The AUTODEPLOY_DISK_PRESSURE journal marker enables countable observability of disk-pressure-triggered reclaims without requiring a new CloudWatch metric
